title: Cal Tjader and Chombo Silva
summary: He criticizes jazz players trying to be Cuban and the reverse.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: To me, I don't want to put it down, but he tried to lean too much on my side. And when you try to lean too much to my side, to me, it was bad music.
Why did he lean towards your side?

He tried to play too much like a Latin. But he didn't have (unintelligible). If he tried to play vibraphone in jazz, and get a real Cuban stuff, in the barrio, then I respect. But he got in between. He got a bass player, and a jazz player tried to play the feeling with the same, with the drum and -- no, I've never (unintelligible).
How about his early recordings with the sax player, what's his name, the Cuban sax player, beautiful sax player --
You didn't. That was, like, the late '50s, they were playing.
There you have the same problem. Chambo -- he don't play Cuban, he tried to play jazz.
So it's like everybody's confused in the middle of the one thing and the other thing. And (unintelli-
You mean, the jazz men are trying to be Cuban and the --
And the Cuban men tried to be jazz. I darn well don't appreciate that.
